brief: Weekly cross-market rates view. Fed Chair Warsh called the recent hike a removal of accommodation rather than tightening, implying the Fed keeps hiking until financial conditions turn restrictive; BofA reads this as hawkish, pays 2Y (entry 4.73%, target 5.25%) and flattens 2s30s, and raises its YE26 2Y and 10Y forecasts to 5.0% from 4.5%. SEP diffusion indices, a 200bp fall in real fed funds versus flat unemployment, and Taylor rule math (5.3-5.4%) all argue the market still underprices the terminal rate, though front-end repricing should pass through to long yields only partially. BoJ's hike is fully priced; its balance sheet is set to shrink fastest among major central banks through 2027, but BofA sees limited near-term repo-rate stress. UK front-end pricing (~4 hikes by mid-2027) looks more hawkish than BofA's own BoE view; the Bank's QT overhaul, pausing active Gilt sales, rallied Gilts. EUR rates are being driven by energy prices, pushing the 10y OAT-Bund spread toward a 100bp break. AU's RBA repricing has turned more hawkish on oil and an expected strong jobs print; BofA stays paid RBA OIS. Canadian inflation held at 3% on gasoline; BofA expects the BoC on hold despite market pricing near five hikes.
